messages:
Marta S.: quick thought — we keep reacting to queue spikes with scale-out, but cold-starts still bite latency. can we separate the "prewarm" signal from the regular autoscaler?
Raj P.: yeah been thinking that too. decouple predictive prewarm from steady-state admission. predictive prewarm should target model warmup + kv cache population.
Kai L.: agree. main question: what signal set do we use for prediction window? queue depth is noisy. tail latency + recent inference miss-rate feels better.
Marta S.: proposal: two pipelines — 1) short-window predictive (10-30s) that triggers prewarm leases, 2) long-window steady autoscale (1-5m) that adjusts pool size. keep independent budgets.
Emilio (infra-bot): note: any pipeline change needs evict-protection hook for Dedicated customers with min-reserve.
Raj P.: also need safety cap on predictive prewarms so multi-tenant burst doesn't exhaust credits. suggest per-tenant prewarm-credit ledger + global reserve.
Anya R.: +1. add hysteresis on prewarm release: don't evict prewarmed pods for at least 45s unless memory pressure critical. avoids churn.
Kai L.: what about using a tiny RL policy to tune prewarm headroom per-tenant based on latency regret? we have historical traces. could bootstrapped as a parameter tuner not full policy.
Marta S.: i'm wary of full RL in control path; prefer supervised tuner that suggests headroom and we keep deterministic fallback. RL for offline optimization only.
Raj P.: fine compromise. practical config example i sketched: 
```
prewarm:
  enabled: true
  predictor: hybrid_tail_latency
  window_seconds: 20
  max_per_tenant: 2
  min_hold_seconds: 45
  budget_key: prewarm_credits
steady_autoscale:
  window_seconds: 120
  target_util: 0.72
  max_scale_per_min: 1.5
```
Kai L.: love that. also add a signal debounce for tail latency so downstream noise (outlier model inferences) doesn't spam prewarms. e.g. require 3/5 windows over threshold.
Anya R.: operational concern: metrics pipelines must expose "prewarm-trigger" event for tracing. ties back to console so tenants see why we prewarmed.
Marta S.: agree. visibility is crucial for debugging cost surprises. annotate requests with reason: predicted|reactive|manual.
Raj P.: eviction priority rules: prewarm < best-effort < reserved. prewarmed hosts are first to be reclaimed. but we must protect active K/V cache on model shards marked pinned.
Kai L.: add compatibility matrix for Dedicated vs Hosted: Dedicated can opt out of predictive prewarm (some enterprise customers hate any extra allocation). Hosted defaults on with opt-out flag.
Emilio (infra-bot): FYI: deploy pipeline has a feature-flag gate for prewarm-experiment. can roll to 5% first.
Anya R.: action items: (1) doc RFC for prewarm pipeline + signals (Marta), (2) implement prewarm-credit ledger + console expose (Raj), (3) add debounce and hold logic in scaler (Kai), (4) tests for eviction ordering + min_hold (Emilio).
Marta S.: i'll draft RFC today. quick note on metrics: include prewarm_success_rate and warm_start_latency delta. those will be our primary evals.
Raj P.: also record cost-per-prewarm and associate to tenant so billing/cost reports can show impact.
Kai L.: small UX ask — in console show a timeline of prewarm events with reason and resulting latency change, per-route. helps product debug regressions.
Anya R.: if we do RL tuning later make sure we persist policy seeds and can audit decisions. no opaque autotune.
Marta S.: agreed. ok I'll start the RFC and ping folks for review. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Emilio (infra-bot): deploy-bot: autoscaler/prewarm v0.1 flagged for rollout to canary group at 03:00 UTC.
